title: Where Does the i Go? Conjugates Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Take 3 + 2i and 3 - 2i. Add them and you get 6. Multiply them and you get 13. Every i vanishes. Why? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) we learn when two complex numbers are equal, and what the conjugate of a complex number is.

You will watch a live match test compare real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts, then see a point z move on the plane while its conjugate z bar follows like a mirror image across the real axis. We put the conjugate and the negative side by side, prove step by step why z + z bar = 2a and z times z bar = a squared + b squared, solve z + 2 z bar = 9 - 4i by equating parts, and fix the exam trap of equating parts too early. Two pause-and-think questions, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Where does the i go?
0:32 When are two complex numbers equal?
1:13 The conjugate: keep the real part, flip the imaginary sign
1:29 Live: z and its mirror image
2:07 Conjugate vs negative
2:44 Why z + z bar and z times z bar are real
3:26 Worked example: z + 2 z bar = 9 - 4i
4:11 Exam trap: collect the parts first
4:33 Where it is asked
4:44 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:26 Recap and three questions to answer
